title: Adaptive transient-slab hints + chunked-KV residency for Llama/Mistral/Qwen long-context tuning
creator: Marta López
description: Problem: For ultra-long contexts (32k+ tokens) across Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants we observe high transient GPU memory spikes during continuous batching and KV growth. Current per-variant memory profiles are statically sized and do not account for transient working sets caused by batching-induced interleaving and model-specific KV access patterns, leading to suboptimal occupancy and unnecessary OOM mitigations.
goal: Produce per-variant memory profile extensions that: 1) expose transient-slab allocator hints for short-lived activations created by batching, 2) implement chunked-KV residency windows (hot/mid/cold) with lightweight compressed representations for cold chunks, and 3) integrate admission/eviction heuristics with the continuous batching scheduler to reduce peak GPU memory and improve throughput without impacting model quality beyond tolerance.
approach:
1) Data collection: run representative traffic traces (chat and long-document generation) for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-1.2-XL, and Qwen-14B with sequence lengths 8k/16k/32k and collect per-layer KV access frequency, allocation lifetimes, and batch interleaving patterns (trace IDs, seed prompts).
2) Analysis: derive per-variant transient hotspot layers and their typical lifetimes; compute optimal transient-slab sizes and candidate thresholds for chunking KV into hot/mid/cold residency.
3) Runtime changes: add transient-slab hint API to allocator; implement chunked-KV residency metadata with optional on-device compression for cold chunks (int8 quantization + delta-encoding for KV vectors); expose eviction/admission hooks to batch scheduler to delay batching of requests that cause high transient overlap.
4) Validation: run GPU occupancy sims and end-to-end perf runs on dedicated pool; measure peak memory, 95/99th latency, throughput (tokens/s), and model output similarity (ROUGE/BLEU/trigger prompts).
5) Rollout: canary on 5% of traffic with automatic rollback if memory SLO or output-quality regressions exceed thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
- Peak GPU memory reduced by >=8% on average and >=5% in p95 across target models/contexts compared to baseline profiles.
- Throughput (tokens/s) improves or stays within +/-3% of baseline for same latency SLO.
- No customer-visible degradation: embedding/prompted-generation quality metrics within tolerated delta (example: mean embedding cosine within 0.01, and generation n-gram precision drop <1%).
- Observability: new metrics (transient_slab_allocs, kv_chunk_evictions, kv_compressed_bytes) appear in Console dashboards and correlate with expected behavior.
- Migration: tooling script to synthesize per-variant profile JSONs from profiler traces included and documented in Confluence.
implementation_steps: Trace collection job (kube job) for target variants: create dataset and attach trace IDs - assigned to Ethan - due 2025-02-25
Profiler analysis notebook: compute layer lifetimes/heatmaps - notebook link in Confluence
Allocator API: transient slab hint interface and unit tests
KV residency metadata: implement chunking + on-device compression path
Batching scheduler integration: admission/eviction hooks and prioritization policy
End-to-end perf runs on dedicated GPU pool and dashboarding
Canary rollout (5%), monitor for 72h, then increase to 25% if stable
notes:
Design trade-offs considered: using compression on cold chunks reduces memory but adds CPU decompress latency — we propose int8 + delta-encode with GPU fast-path for common shapes to minimize overhead. Alternative was to expand host-side spill which increases PCIe traffic and latency. Chosen path favors latency-sensitive workloads.
We will keep a 'cold switch' threshold tunable by release flags to quickly flip behavior for specific customers (Dedicated/Private deployments).
